exposure: Management practices (tranexamic acid, oxytocin/misoprostol, uterine massage)
outcome: Maternal near-misses (hysterectomy, cardiovascular dysfunction, uterine rupture, massive blood loss)
Critical interventions (intensive care, laparotomy, blood transfusions)
cohort: The study included 60 women experiencing severe postpartum haemorrhage, consisting of both in-house patients and referrals, at Kawempe National Referral Hospital in Uganda.
finding: Referral patients with severe PPH were found to be more critically ill and disproportionately affected by adverse outcomes and substandard care, particularly regarding non-pharmaceutical interventions, despite timely administration of drugs and fluids according to national guidelines.
